A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SafeDialBench study. Their main text, Appendices A-G, tables, figures and evaluation examples are available and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 17 LLMs, attack and dialogue-turn analyses, and assessments by five human experts on 100 dialogues (Section 4 and Appendix G).

after.justification: v3 retains the original model evaluations, supplementary analyses and human-assessment results in Section 4 and Appendix G.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, seven attack strategies, three safety abilities, golden dialogue histories and minimum-over-turn scoring remain unchanged. The temperature revision concerns evaluation settings rather than a proposed method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 4,053 Chinese and English dialogues covering six safety dimensions, 22 scenarios, seven attack strategies and 3-10 turns. Appendix D and Table 7 retain the same coverage and counts.

E2.justification: The evaluated model membership remains unchanged in Tables 2-3 and 9-11, including English-only Llama3.1-8B-Instruct. GPT-3.5 turbo, Qwen-72B and human experts retain their evaluation roles.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the stated temperature for each evaluated LLM from 0.7 in v1 to 0 in v3. Other evaluation settings remain unchanged. This is a reported protocol revision; neither PDF establishes that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The attack comparisons, per-turn analysis, model-size analysis, human-evaluator agreement analysis and case studies remain unchanged in Sections 4.2-4.3 and Appendix G.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The human-agreement reporting in Table 4 and the plots' reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 2-4 and 9-11 retain identical numerical results, and the result plots and case outcomes are unchanged. No updated outcomes accompany the temperature revision, so the PDFs do not demonstrate a same-setting performance difference.

T1.justification: The taxonomy, capability definitions and scoring rule are unchanged. Neither version contains a formal theoretical development, theorem or proof that is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark and evaluation-framework contributions, model-safety claims and claims about effective jailbreak strategies.

C2.justification: The interpretations of attack effectiveness, model size, language differences and evaluator agreement are unchanged. Sections 6-7 retain the same limitations concerning attack coverage, dataset updates, assessment granularity and cultural coverage.

D1.justification: The documented temperature changes from 0.7 to 0 in Section 4.1. Data-construction instructions, evaluation prompts, model-access information and the dataset link otherwise remain unchanged; no explanation identifies this as a reporting correction or an actual experimental change.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix A, benchmark-comparison Tables 1 and 5, and the references retain the same cited works and research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 adds affiliation 4 to Boyan Wang, Tianpei Yang and Yang Gao and updates the arXiv version/date text. Scientific prose and the organization of the main sections and appendices are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: There are small first-page formatting changes to the author line and arXiv margin stamp, plus minor typesetting shifts. All 19 figures and 11 tables retain their content, structure, captions and placement.

improvement.justification: The scientific evidence, arguments and limitations are unchanged. The only scientific revision is the unexplained temperature change from 0.7 to 0 in Section 4.1, with identical reported results. The PDFs do not establish whether this makes the protocol description more accurate or introduces an inconsistency. The affiliation and formatting edits do not resolve that uncertainty about overall quality.
